edges.description: GABA-A receptor subunit variants reduce inhibitory GABAergic signaling.
EFHC1 variants perturb neuronal excitability and cortical development.
A truncating CACNB4 variant reported in a JME patient alters the gating of the calcium channel it assembles with.

edges.description: Reduced inhibition disinhibits cortical and thalamocortical networks.
EFHC1-related dysregulation contributes to cortical hyperexcitability.
Altered calcium-channel gating is proposed to contribute to cortical network hyperexcitability; the cited study measured channel kinetics only and did not show a network effect.

edges.description: Cortical/thalamocortical hypersynchrony produces generalized polyspike-wave discharges.
Generalized polyspike-wave discharges produce the clinical seizures.
Generalized thalamocortical polyspike-and-wave discharges register on scalp electroencephalography as 4-6 Hz polyspike-wave complexes.
Visual-thalamocortical hyperexcitability manifests on intermittent photic stimulation as a photoparoxysmal EEG response.
Motor-predominant generalized discharges on awakening produce bilateral upper-limb myoclonic seizures.
Sustained generalized hypersynchronous recruitment produces bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, often preceded by clustered morning myoclonias.
Generalized spike-and-wave network oscillations produce brief typical absence seizures in a subset of patients.

nodes.description: Excess alcohol intake is a classic external seizure precipitant in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, frequently provoking morning myoclonic flurries and generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

evidence.snippet: Approximately two-thirds of the patients with JME report that seizures are provoked by a variety of general factors like stress, fatigue, fever, and sleep and more specific precipitants like flashing sunlight, music, reading, thinking, and excess alcohol.

evidence.reference_title: Coding and noncoding variation of the human calcium-channel beta4-subunit gene CACNB4 in patients with idiopathic generalized epilepsy and episodic ataxia.
evidence.snippet: The premature-termination mutation R482X was identified in a patient with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.

nodes.description: CACNB4 encodes the beta-4 auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, which regulates the gating of the pore-forming alpha1 subunit. The truncating p.Arg482Ter variant reported in a JME patient alters alpha1 inactivation kinetics in vitro. This node captures the altered regulation of calcium-channel gating by the beta-4 subunit; it is a separate mechanism from the EFHC1 arm.

evidence.snippet: The results of functional tests of the truncated protein R482X in Xenopus laevis oocytes demonstrated a small decrease in the fast time constant for inactivation of the cotransfected alpha1 subunit.

nodes.description: The motor cortex and the reciprocal thalamocortical network become hyperexcitable and prone to hypersynchronous discharge, with particular involvement of frontal/motor systems. This node captures the single concept of network hyperexcitability and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in EFHC1 cause juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Mutation analyses identified five missense mutations in EFHC1 that cosegregated with epilepsy or EEG polyspike wave in affected members of six unrelated families with JME and did not occur in 382 control individuals

evidence.reference_title: EFHC1 variants in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy: reanalysis according to NHGRI and ACMG guidelines for assigning disease causality.

nodes.description: EFHC1 (myoclonin1) is a non-ion-channel protein that modulates R-type calcium currents and has been implicated in neuronal division and migration; JME-associated EFHC1 variants reverse its effect on R-type currents and perturb cortical neuronal excitability. This node captures the EFHC1 arm only.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in EFHC1 cause juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report that genetic variation within the GABRD gene, which encodes the GABAA receptor delta subunit, affects GABA current amplitude consistent with a model of polygenic susceptibility to epilepsy in humans.

nodes.description: JME has a strong, usually complex (polygenic) genetic basis. Susceptibility variants affect GABA-A receptor subunits (GABRA1, GABRD), the EFHC1 (myoclonin) gene, and calcium-channel subunits (CACNB4), shifting the excitation-inhibition balance of cortical and thalamocortical circuits. This node captures the single concept of the predisposing genetic variation.

Reduced GABA-A receptor-mediated inhibition (e.g., from GABRA1 or GABRD variants) lowers the inhibitory restraint on cortical neurons. This node captures the single concept of the inhibitory deficit and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

nodes.description: The clinical seizures are early-morning myoclonic jerks (especially of the upper limbs, shortly after awakening), generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and typical absence seizures in a subset. Seizures are provoked by sleep deprivation, alcohol, and fatigue. This node captures the single concept of the seizure endpoint and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

A photoparoxysmal EEG response to intermittent photic stimulation is common in JME. The evidence below quantifies the EEG trait; the rate of seizures actually provoked by flickering light is not separately established here.
